quick: Take with or after food to reduce GI upset
Avoid, especially in third trimester (NSAID class risk)
GI symptoms, renal function, blood pressure
summary: Zaltoprofen is a propionic acid derivative NSAID used to relieve pain and inflammation in osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, low back pain, periarthritis of the shoulder, and post-surgical, post-traumatic, and post-extraction pain. The usual adult dose is 80 mg three times daily (up to 240 mg/day). It inhibits cyclooxygenase-mediated prostaglandin synthesis and also suppresses bradykinin-induced pain. Like other NSAIDs it carries class risks of gastrointestinal, renal, and cardiovascular adverse effects. It is marketed mainly in Japan and parts of Asia and is not FDA-approved.
indications: Pain and inflammation of rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis
Low back pain, periarthritis of the shoulder, and neck-shoulder-arm syndrome
Pain and inflammation following surgery, trauma, or tooth extraction

dosage.d: 80 mg as a single dose, may repeat; 80-160 mg per dose
dosage.n: Up to 240 mg/day; use lowest effective dose for shortest time

dosage.d: Use the lowest effective dose with monitoring

admin: Take orally with or after food to reduce gastrointestinal irritation
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals
Ensure adequate hydration, especially in elderly or those with renal risk
moa: Zaltoprofen is a propionic acid derivative NSAID that inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2) enzymes, reducing synthesis of prostaglandins that mediate pain, inflammation, and fever. In addition to prostaglandin inhibition, it suppresses bradykinin-induced pain responses (inhibition of bradykinin-stimulated nociceptive signaling), which contributes to its analgesic effect.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to zaltoprofen or other NSAIDs
History of aspirin/NSAID-induced asthma, urticaria, or allergic-type reactions
Active peptic ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding

preg: As with other NSAIDs, avoid in pregnancy, particularly in the third trimester, due to the risk of premature closure of the ductus arteriosus, fetal renal impairment, and impaired labor. Use earlier in pregnancy only if clearly necessary.
lact: NSAIDs are excreted into breast milk. Avoid use during breastfeeding or choose an alternative; if used, monitor the infant.
renal: NSAIDs can reduce renal perfusion and precipitate acute kidney injury. Avoid in significant renal impairment, use with caution in mild-moderate impairment, ensure hydration, and monitor renal function.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; NSAIDs can rarely cause hepatotoxicity. Avoid in severe impairment and monitor liver enzymes with prolonged use.

major: Anticoagulants (warfarin, DOACs) and antiplatelets - increased bleeding risk
Other NSAIDs/aspirin - additive GI toxicity and bleeding
Methotrexate - reduced clearance and increased toxicity
moderate: ACE inhibitors/ARBs and diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect and risk of acute kidney injury (triple whammy)
Lithium - reduced renal clearance and increased levels
minor: Quinolone antibiotics - theoretical lowering of seizure threshold
interactions.food: Take with or after food to reduce gastric irritation.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - increases risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
interactions.diagnostics: May affect renal function tests and, rarely, liver enzymes; can mask fever and inflammation markers.

monitoring: Gastrointestinal symptoms and signs of bleeding
Hemoglobin in patients at bleeding risk
counsel: Take with or after food and use the lowest dose for the shortest time needed
Stop and seek care if you have black stools, vomiting blood, or severe stomach pain
Avoid alcohol and other anti-inflammatory painkillers
Report swelling, breathlessness, reduced urination, or rash
Tell your doctor if you have heart, kidney, liver, or stomach problems or are pregnant
pk: Store below 30 C in a dry place, protected from light
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; authored from international (Japan/Asia) product information and published reviews
Propionic acid NSAID that also inhibits bradykinin-mediated pain in addition to COX inhibition
Carries the full NSAID class risk profile - GI, renal, and cardiovascular
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration; co-prescribe a PPI in high GI-risk patients
Avoid in third-trimester pregnancy and in aspirin/NSAID-sensitive asthma
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose. For as-needed use, take only when pain is present.
overdose: Overdose may cause nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, GI bleeding, drowsiness, headache, and rarely seizures, hypotension, or renal failure. There is no specific antidote; manage supportively with gastric decontamination if recent and large, fluids, and monitoring of renal and GI status. NSAIDs are not effectively removed by dialysis.
